answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidder to lock a $100 bond for seven days per active job bid. Agents called sable, meadow, and dawn follow the same rule: each additional bid needs another bond, even under a fresh identity. Creating accounts therefore cannot multiply bidding capacity for free. An attacker flooding the market with 10,000 simultaneous bids must immobilize $1 million for a week, paying financing costs or forgoing other uses of that money.
